entities.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיְדַבֵּר and identifies God as the speaker addressing Noah.
God addresses נֹחַ after the flood. The addressee is the flood survivor, son of Lamech.

name_review_base.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיְדַבֵּר and identifies God as the speaker addressing Noah.
God addresses נֹחַ after the flood. The addressee is the flood survivor, son of Lamech.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject, אֶל נֹחַ identifies Noah as the addressee, and לֵאמֹר introduces what God said.
analysis.morphology: Piel wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיְדַבֵּר, the third-person masculine singular verb “he spoke.” The singular agreement identifies God as the speaker, and אֶל נֹחַ identifies Noah as the addressee.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְדַבֵּר אֱלֹהִים אֶל נֹחַ, God speaks and אֶל introduces Noah as the person addressed.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Marks the person or people addressed.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיְדַבֵּר אֱלֹהִים אֶל נֹחַ, “God spoke to Noah,” the preposition אֶל introduces נֹחַ as the person God addresses.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וַיְדַבֵּר אֱלֹהִים אֶל נֹחַ identifies God as the speaker and Noah as the addressee. לֵאמֹר introduces the words God speaks to Noah.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with prefixed preposition לְ, realized as לֵ־
